segs.e: Numbered Discourses 2.1–10
The Chapter on Punishments
1. Faults
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“There are, mendicants, these two faults.
What two?
The fault apparent in this life, and the fault to do with lives to come.
What is the fault apparent in this life?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco passati coraṁ āgucāriṁ rājāno gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārente;
segs.e: It’s when someone sees that kings have arrested a bandit, a criminal, and subjected them to various punishments—

segs.p: kasāhipi tāḷente, vettehipi tāḷente, addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷente, hatthampi chindante, pādampi chindante, hatthapādampi chindante, kaṇṇampi chindante, nāsampi chindante, kaṇṇanāsampi chindante, bilaṅgathālikampi karonte, saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonte, rāhumukhampi karonte, jotimālikampi karonte, hatthapajjotikampi karonte, erakavattikampi karonte, cīrakavāsikampi karonte, eṇeyyakampi karonte, baḷisamaṁsikampi karonte, kahāpaṇikampi karonte, khārāpatacchikampi karonte, palighaparivattikampi karonte, palālapīṭhakampi karonte, tattenapi telena osiñcante, sunakhehipi khādāpente, jīvantampi sūle uttāsente, asināpi sīsaṁ chindante.
segs.e: whipping, caning, and clubbing; cutting off hands or feet, or both; cutting off ears or nose, or both; the ‘porridge pot’, the ‘shell-shave’, the ‘Rāhu’s mouth’, the ‘garland of fire’, the ‘burning hand’, the ‘bulrush twist’, the ‘bark dress’, the ‘antelope’, the ‘meat hook’, the ‘coins’, the ‘caustic pickle’, the ‘twisting bar’, the ‘straw mat’; being splashed with hot oil, being fed to the hounds, being impaled alive, and being beheaded.
It occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘yathārūpānaṁ kho pāpakānaṁ kammānaṁ hetu coraṁ āgucāriṁ rājāno gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārenti;
segs.e: ‘If I were to commit the kinds of bad deeds for which the kings arrested that bandit, that criminal,

segs.p: kasāhipi tāḷenti, vettehipi tāḷenti, addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷenti, hatthampi chindanti, pādampi chindanti, hatthapādampi chindanti, kaṇṇampi chindanti, nāsampi chindanti, kaṇṇanāsampi chindanti, bilaṅgathālikampi karonti, saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonti, rāhumukhampi karonti, jotimālikampi karonti, hatthapajjotikampi karonti, erakavattikampi karonti, cīrakavāsikampi karonti, eṇeyyakampi karonti, baḷisamaṁsikampi karonti, kahāpaṇikampi karonti, khārāpatacchikampi karonti, palighaparivattikampi karonti, palālapīṭhakampi karonti, tattenapi telena osiñcanti, sunakhehipi khādāpenti, jīvantampi sūle uttāsenti, asināpi sīsaṁ chindanti.
Ahañceva kho pana evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ kareyyaṁ, mampi rājāno gahetvā evarūpā vividhā kammakāraṇā kāreyyuṁ;
segs.e: the rulers would arrest me and subject me to the same punishments.’

segs.p: So diṭṭhadhammikassa vajjassa bhīto na paresaṁ pābhataṁ vilumpanto carati.
segs.e: Afraid of the fault apparent in this life, they do not steal the belongings of others.
This is called the fault apparent in this life.
What is the fault to do with lives to come?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘kāyaduccaritassa kho pana pāpako dukkho vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ, vacīduccaritassa pāpako dukkho vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ, manoduccaritassa pāpako dukkho vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad, painful result in the next life.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana kāyena duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, vācāya duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, manasā duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ.
segs.e: If I conduct myself badly,

segs.p: Kiñca taṁ yāhaṁ na kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: then, when my body breaks up, after death, won’t I be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?’

segs.p: So samparāyikassa vajjassa bhīto kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Afraid of the fault to do with lives to come, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the fault to do with lives to come.
These are the two faults.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘diṭṭhadhammikassa vajjassa bhāyissāma, samparāyikassa vajjassa bhāyissāma, vajjabhīruno bhavissāma vajjabhayadassāvino’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will fear the fault apparent in this life, and we will fear the fault to do with lives to come. We will fear faults, seeing the danger in faults.’
That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Vajjabhīruno, bhikkhave, vajjabhayadassāvino etaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ yaṁ parimuccissati sabbavajjehī”ti.
segs.e: If you fear faults, seeing the danger in faults, you can expect to be freed from all faults.”
2. Endeavor
“These two endeavors are challenging in the world.
What two?

segs.p: Yañca gihīnaṁ agāraṁ ajjhāvasataṁ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānatthaṁ padhānaṁ, yañca agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitānaṁ sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggatthaṁ padhānaṁ.
segs.e: The endeavor of laypeople staying in a home to provide robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And the endeavor of those gone forth from the lay life to homelessness to let go of all attachments.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dve padhānāni durabhisambhavāni lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the two endeavors that are challenging in the world.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ padhānānaṁ yadidaṁ sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggatthaṁ padhānaṁ.
segs.e: The better of these two endeavors is the effort to let go of all attachments.
So you should train like this:
‘We shall endeavor to let go of all attachments.’
That’s how you should train.”
3. Mortifying
“These two things, mendicants, are mortifying.
What two?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa kāyaduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti kāyasucaritaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when someone has done bad things and not done good things, by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: vacīduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti vacīsucaritaṁ;
manoduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti manosucaritaṁ.
So ‘kāyaduccaritaṁ me katan’ti tappati, ‘akataṁ me kāyasucaritan’ti tappati;
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I’ve done bad things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re mortified. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done good things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re mortified.

segs.p: ‘vacīduccaritaṁ me katan’ti tappati, ‘akataṁ me vacīsucaritan’ti tappati;
‘manoduccaritaṁ me katan’ti tappati, ‘akataṁ me manosucaritan’ti tappati.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā tapanīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are mortifying.”
4. Not Mortifying
“These two things, mendicants, are not mortifying.
What two?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa kāyasucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti kāyaduccaritaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when someone has done good things and not done bad things, by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: vacīsucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti vacīduccaritaṁ;
manosucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti manoduccaritaṁ.
So ‘kāyasucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me kāyaduccaritan’ti na tappati;
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I’ve done good things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re not mortified. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done bad things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re not mortified.

segs.p: ‘vacīsucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me vacīduccaritan’ti na tappati;
‘manosucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me manoduccaritan’ti na tappati.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā atapanīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are not mortifying.”
5. Learned for Myself
“Mendicants, I have learned these two things for myself—

segs.p: yā ca asantuṭṭhitā kusalesu dhammesu, yā ca appaṭivānitā padhānasmiṁ.
segs.e: to never be content with skillful qualities, and to never stop trying.
I never stopped trying, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ, yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and bones remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, appamādādhigatā sambodhi, appamādādhigato anuttaro yogakkhemo.
segs.e: It was by diligence that I achieved awakening, and by diligence that I achieved the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
If you too never stop trying, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ, yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti, tumhepi, bhikkhave, nacirasseva—
segs.e: ‘Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and bones remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

segs.p: yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatha.
segs.e: You will soon realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. You will live having achieved with your own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.
So you should train like this:
‘We will never stop trying, thinking:

segs.p: Kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ, yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: “Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and bones remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.”’
That’s how you should train.”
6. Fetters
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?

segs.p: Yā ca saṁyojaniyesu dhammesu assādānupassitā, yā ca saṁyojaniyesu dhammesu nibbidānupassitā.
segs.e: Seeing things that tighten the fetters as gratifying, and seeing things that tighten the fetters as boring.

segs.p: Saṁyojaniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu assādānupassī viharanto rāgaṁ na pajahati, dosaṁ na pajahati, mohaṁ na pajahati.
segs.e: When you keep seeing things that tighten the fetters as gratifying, you don’t give up greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Rāgaṁ appahāya, dosaṁ appahāya, mohaṁ appahāya na parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: When these are not given up, you’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
You’re not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Saṁyojaniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu nibbidānupassī viharanto rāgaṁ pajahati, dosaṁ pajahati, mohaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: When you keep seeing things that tighten the fetters as boring, you give up greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Rāgaṁ pahāya, dosaṁ pahāya, mohaṁ pahāya, parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: When these are given up, you’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
You’re freed from suffering, I say.
These are the two things.”
7. Dark
“These two things, mendicants, are dark.
What two?
Lack of conscience and prudence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā kaṇhā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are dark.”
8. Bright
“These two things, mendicants, are bright.
What two?
Conscience and prudence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā sukkā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are bright.”
9. Conduct
“These two bright things, mendicants, protect the world.
What two?
Conscience and prudence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve sukkā dhammā lokaṁ na pāleyyuṁ, nayidha paññāyetha mātāti vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṁ dārāti vā.
segs.e: If these two bright things did not protect the world, there would be no recognition of the status of mother, aunts, or wives and partners of tutors and respected people.

segs.p: Sambhedaṁ loko agamissa, yathā ajeḷakā kukkuṭasūkarā soṇasiṅgālā.
segs.e: The world would become dissolute, like goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and hounds and jackals.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, ime dve sukkā dhammā lokaṁ pālenti tasmā paññāyati mātāti vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṁ dārāti vā”ti.
segs.e: But because the two bright things protect the world, there is recognition of the status of mother, aunts, and wives and partners of tutors and respected people.”
10. Entering the Rainy Season
“There are, mendicants, these two entries to the rainy season.
What two?
Earlier and later.
These are the two entries to the rainy season.”
Numbered Discourses 2.11–20
The Chapter on Disciplinary Issues
“There are, mendicants, these two powers.
What two?
The power of reflection and the power of development.
And what, mendicants, is the power of reflection?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘kāyaduccaritassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca, vacīduccaritassa pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca, manoduccaritassa pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad, painful result in both this life and the next.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the power of reflection.
And what, mendicants, is the power of development?

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ bhāvanābalaṁ sekhānametaṁ balaṁ.
segs.e: In this context, the power of development is the power of the trainees.

segs.p: Sekhañhi so, bhikkhave, balaṁ āgamma rāgaṁ pajahati, dosaṁ pajahati, mohaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: For when you rely on the power of a trainee, you give up greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: Rāgaṁ pahāya, dosaṁ pahāya, mohaṁ pahāya yaṁ akusalaṁ na taṁ karoti, yaṁ pāpaṁ na taṁ sevati.
segs.e: Then you don’t do anything unskillful, or practice anything bad.
This is called the power of development.
These are the two powers.”

It’s when someone reflects:

segs.e: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad, painful result in both this life and the next.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the power of reflection.
And what, mendicants, is the power of development?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vosaggapariṇāmiṁ,
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness,
investigation of principles,
energy,
rapture,
tranquility,
immersion,

segs.p: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vosaggapariṇāmiṁ.
segs.e: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
This is called the power of development.
These are the two powers.”
“There are, mendicants, these two powers.
What two?
The power of reflection and the power of development.
And what, mendicants, is the power of reflection?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘kāyaduccaritassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca, vacīduccaritassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca, manoduccaritassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad, painful result in both this life and the next.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the power of reflection.
And what, mendicants, is the power of development?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segs.p: Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.
This is called the power of development.
These are the two powers.”
“Mendicants, the Realized One has two ways of teaching the Dhamma.
What two?
In brief and in detail.

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgatassa dhammadesanā”ti.
segs.e: These are the Realized One’s two ways of teaching the Dhamma.”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu na sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a disciplinary issue, if neither the offending mendicant nor the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue

segs.p: ‘dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca na phāsuṁ viharissantī’ti.
segs.e: will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants won’t live comfortably.

segs.p: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: But in a disciplinary issue, if both the offending mendicant and the accusing mendicant carefully check themselves, you can expect that issue

segs.p: ‘na dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca phāsuṁ viharissantī’ti.
segs.e: won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati?
segs.e: And how, mendicants, does an offending mendicant carefully check themselves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: An offending mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: ‘I have committed a certain unskillful offense with the body.

segs.p: Maṁ so bhikkhu addasa akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: That mendicant saw me do this.

segs.p: No ce ahaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjeyyaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, na maṁ so bhikkhu passeyya akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: If I hadn’t committed that offense, they wouldn’t have seen me.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, ahaṁ akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, tasmā maṁ so bhikkhu addasa akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: But since I did commit that offense, they did see me.

segs.p: Disvā ca pana maṁ so bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena anattamano ahosi.
segs.e: When they saw me, they were upset,

segs.p: Anattamano samāno anattamanavacanaṁ maṁ so bhikkhu avaca.
segs.e: and they voiced their unhappiness to me.

segs.p: Anattamanavacanāhaṁ tena bhikkhunā vutto samāno anattamano ahosiṁ.
segs.e: Then I also got upset,
so I told others.

segs.p: Iti mameva tattha accayo accagamā suṅkadāyakaṁva bhaṇḍasmin’ti.
segs.e: So the mistake is mine alone, like someone who owes customs duty on their goods.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, āpanno bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati.
segs.e: That’s how, mendicants, an offending mendicant carefully checks themselves.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati?
segs.e: And how, mendicants, does an accusing mendicant carefully check themselves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: An accusing mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: ‘This mendicant has committed a certain unskillful offense with the body.

segs.p: Ahaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ addasaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: I saw them do that.

segs.p: No ce ayaṁ bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpajjeyya kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, nāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ passeyyaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: If they hadn’t committed that offense, I wouldn’t have seen them.

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, ayaṁ bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno kañcideva desaṁ kāyena, tasmā ahaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ addasaṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena.
segs.e: But since they did commit that offense, I did see them.

segs.p: Disvā ca panāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ akusalaṁ āpajjamānaṁ kañcideva desaṁ kāyena anattamano ahosiṁ.
segs.e: When I saw them, I was upset,

segs.p: Anattamano samāno anattamanavacanāhaṁ imaṁ bhikkhuṁ avacaṁ.
segs.e: and I voiced my unhappiness to them.

segs.p: Anattamanavacanāyaṁ bhikkhu mayā vutto samāno anattamano ahosi.
segs.e: Then they also got upset,
so they told others.

segs.p: Iti mameva tattha accayo accagamā suṅkadāyakaṁva bhaṇḍasmin’ti.
segs.e: So the mistake is mine alone, like someone who owes customs duty on their goods.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati.
segs.e: That’s how, mendicants, an accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu na sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca na phāsuṁ viharissantīti.
segs.e: In a disciplinary issue, if neither the offending mendicant nor the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants won’t live comfortably.

segs.p: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe āpanno ca bhikkhu codako ca bhikkhu sādhukaṁ attanāva attānaṁ paccavekkhati tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ na dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca phāsuṁ viharissantī”ti.
segs.e: But in a disciplinary issue, if both the offending mendicant and the accusing mendicant carefully checks themselves, you can expect that issue won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.”

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”

segs.p: “Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: “Unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”

segs.p: “Dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: “Principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he was righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”
“What they’ve done and what they’ve not done.

segs.p: Evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: “Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti?
segs.e: “But what is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”
“What they’ve done and what they’ve not done.

segs.p: Evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Na kho ahaṁ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “I don’t understand the meaning of what the worthy Gotama has said in brief, without explaining the details.

segs.p: Sādhu me bhavaṁ gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā ahaṁ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājāneyyan”ti.
segs.e: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this matter in detail so I can understand the meaning.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” Jānussoṇi replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekaccassa kāyaduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti kāyasucaritaṁ;
segs.e: “Firstly, brahmin, someone has done bad things and not done good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: vacīduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti vacīsucaritaṁ;
manoduccaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti manosucaritaṁ.
Evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, katattā ca akatattā ca evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: So what they’ve done and what they’ve not done is why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekaccassa kāyasucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti kāyaduccaritaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, brahmin, someone has done good things and not done bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: vacīsucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti vacīduccaritaṁ;
manosucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti manoduccaritaṁ.
Evaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, katattā ca akatattā ca evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: So what they’ve done and what they’ve not done is why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! … From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “ekaṁsenāhaṁ, ānanda, akaraṇīyaṁ vadāmi kāyaduccaritaṁ vacīduccaritaṁ manoduccaritan”ti.
segs.e: “Ānanda, I absolutely say that you should not do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.”

segs.p: “Yamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā ekaṁsena akaraṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyaduccaritaṁ vacīduccaritaṁ manoduccaritaṁ tasmiṁ akaraṇīye kayiramāne ko ādīnavo pāṭikaṅkho”ti?
segs.e: “But, sir, if someone does these things that should not be done, what drawbacks should they expect?”

segs.p: “Yamidaṁ, ānanda, mayā ekaṁsena akaraṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyaduccaritaṁ vacīduccaritaṁ manoduccaritaṁ tasmiṁ akaraṇīye kayiramāne ayaṁ ādīnavo pāṭikaṅkho—
segs.e: “They should expect these drawbacks.
They blame themselves.
After examination, sensible people criticize them.
They get a bad reputation.
They feel lost when they die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: And when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yamidaṁ, ānanda, mayā ekaṁsena akaraṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyaduccaritaṁ vacīduccaritaṁ manoduccaritaṁ tasmiṁ akaraṇīye kayiramāne ayaṁ ādīnavo pāṭikaṅkho”ti.
segs.e: These are the drawbacks they should expect.”

segs.p: “Ekaṁsenāhaṁ, ānanda, karaṇīyaṁ vadāmi kāyasucaritaṁ vacīsucaritaṁ manosucaritan”ti.
segs.e: “Ānanda, I absolutely say that you should do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.”

segs.p: “Yamidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā ekaṁsena karaṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyasucaritaṁ vacīsucaritaṁ manosucaritaṁ tasmiṁ karaṇīye kayiramāne ko ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho”ti?
segs.e: “But, sir, if someone does these things that should be done, what benefits should they expect?”

segs.p: “Yamidaṁ, ānanda, mayā ekaṁsena karaṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyasucaritaṁ vacīsucaritaṁ manosucaritaṁ tasmiṁ karaṇīye kayiramāne ayaṁ ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho—
segs.e: “They should expect these benefits.
They don’t blame themselves.
After examination, sensible people praise them.
They get a good reputation.
They don’t feel lost when they die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: And when the body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Yamidaṁ, ānanda, mayā ekaṁsena karaṇīyaṁ akkhātaṁ kāyasucaritaṁ vacīsucaritaṁ manosucaritaṁ tasmiṁ karaṇīye kayiramāne ayaṁ ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho”ti.
segs.e: These are the benefits they should expect.”
“Mendicants, give up the unskillful.
It is possible to give up the unskillful.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, sakkā abhavissa akusalaṁ pajahituṁ, nāhaṁ evaṁ vadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If it wasn’t possible, I wouldn’t say:
‘Give up the unskillful.’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, sakkā akusalaṁ pajahituṁ tasmāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: But it is possible, and so I say:
‘Give up the unskillful.’

segs.p: Akusalañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, pahīnaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvatteyya nāhaṁ evaṁ vadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: And if giving up the unskillful led to harm and suffering, I would not say:
‘Give up the unskillful.’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, akusalaṁ pahīnaṁ hitāya sukhāya saṁvattati tasmāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: But giving up the unskillful leads to welfare and happiness, so I say:
‘Give up the unskillful.’
Mendicants, develop the skillful.
It is possible to develop the skillful.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, sakkā abhavissa kusalaṁ bhāvetuṁ, nāhaṁ evaṁ vadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If it wasn’t possible, I wouldn’t say:
‘Develop the skillful.’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, sakkā kusalaṁ bhāvetuṁ tasmāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: But it is possible, and so I say:
‘Develop the skillful.’

segs.p: Kusalañca hidaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvatteyya, nāhaṁ evaṁ vadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If developing the skillful led to harm and suffering I wouldn’t say:
‘Develop the skillful.’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, kusalaṁ bhāvitaṁ hitāya sukhāya saṁvattati tasmāhaṁ evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: But developing the skillful leads to welfare and happiness, so I say:
‘Develop the skillful.’”

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These two things, mendicants, lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.
What two?
The words and phrases are misplaced, and the meaning is misinterpreted.

segs.p: Dunnikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi dunnayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are misplaced, the meaning is misinterpreted.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These two things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These two things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.
What two?
The words and phrases are well organized, and the meaning is correctly interpreted.

segs.p: Sunikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi sunayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are well organized, the meaning is correctly interpreted.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These two things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 2.21–31
The Chapter on Fools
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca accayaṁ accayato na passati, yo ca accayaṁ desentassa yathādhammaṁ nappaṭiggaṇhāti.
segs.e: One who doesn’t recognize when they’ve made a mistake. And one who doesn’t properly accept the confession of someone who’s made a mistake.
These are the two fools.
There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca accayaṁ accayato passati, yo ca accayaṁ desentassa yathādhammaṁ paṭiggaṇhāti.
segs.e: One who recognizes when they’ve made a mistake. And one who properly accepts the confession of someone who’s made a mistake.
These are the two who are astute.”
“Mendicants, these two misrepresent the Realized One.
What two?

segs.p: Duṭṭho vā dosantaro, saddho vā duggahitena.
segs.e: One who is hateful and hides it, and one whose faith is mistaken.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgataṁ abbhācikkhantī”ti.
segs.e: These two misrepresent the Realized One.”
“Mendicants, these two misrepresent the Realized One.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatena bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, yo ca bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatena abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpeti.
segs.e: One who explains what was not spoken by the Realized One as spoken by him. And one who explains what was spoken by the Realized One as not spoken by him.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgataṁ abbhācikkhantīti.
segs.e: These two misrepresent the Realized One.
These two don’t misrepresent the Realized One.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatena abhāsitaṁ alapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, yo ca bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatena bhāsitaṁ lapitaṁ tathāgatenāti dīpeti.
segs.e: One who explains what was not spoken by the Realized One as not spoken by him. And one who explains what was spoken by the Realized One as spoken by him.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgataṁ nābbhācikkhantī”ti.
segs.e: These two don’t misrepresent the Realized One.”
“Mendicants, these two misrepresent the Realized One.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca neyyatthaṁ suttantaṁ nītattho suttantoti dīpeti, yo ca nītatthaṁ suttantaṁ neyyattho suttantoti dīpeti.
segs.e: One who explains a discourse in need of interpretation as a discourse whose meaning is explicit. And one who explains a discourse whose meaning is explicit as a discourse in need of interpretation.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgataṁ abbhācikkhantī”ti.
segs.e: These two misrepresent the Realized One.”
“These two don’t misrepresent the Realized One.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca neyyatthaṁ suttantaṁ neyyattho suttantoti dīpeti, yo ca nītatthaṁ suttantaṁ nītattho suttantoti dīpeti.
segs.e: One who explains a discourse in need of interpretation as a discourse in need of interpretation. And one who explains a discourse whose meaning is explicit as a discourse whose meaning is explicit.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve tathāgataṁ nābbhācikkhantī”ti.
segs.e: These two don’t misrepresent the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Paṭicchannakammantassa, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññatarā gati pāṭikaṅkhā—
segs.e: “Mendicants, one who is underhand can expect one of two destinies:
hell or the animal realm.

segs.p: Appaṭicchannakammantassa, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññatarā gati pāṭikaṅkhā—
segs.e: One who is aboveboard can expect one of two destinies:
as a god or a human.”

segs.p: “Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññatarā gati pāṭikaṅkhā—
segs.e: “Mendicants, one who has wrong view can expect one of two destinies:
hell or the animal realm.”

segs.p: “Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññatarā gati pāṭikaṅkhā—
segs.e: “Mendicants, one who has right view can expect one of two destinies:
as a god or a human.”
“There are two places waiting to receive an unethical person:
hell and the animal realm.
There are two places waiting to receive an ethical person:
the realms of gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Dvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, atthavase sampassamāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I see two reasons to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.
What two?

segs.p: Attano ca diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṁ sampassamāno, pacchimañca janataṁ anukampamāno.
segs.e: Seeing happiness for oneself in this life, and having sympathy for future generations.

segs.p: Ime kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, dve atthavase sampassamāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmī”ti.
segs.e: I see two reasons to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”
“These two things play a part in realization.
What two?
Serenity and discernment.
What is the benefit of developing serenity?
The mind is developed.
What is the benefit of developing the mind?
Greed is given up.
What is the benefit of developing discernment?
Wisdom is developed.
What is the benefit of developing wisdom?
Ignorance is given up.

segs.p: Rāgupakkiliṭṭhaṁ vā, bhikkhave, cittaṁ na vimuccati, avijjupakkiliṭṭhā vā paññā na bhāvīyati.
segs.e: The mind corrupted by greed is not free; and wisdom corrupted by ignorance does not grow.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, rāgavirāgā cetovimutti, avijjāvirāgā paññāvimuttī”ti.
segs.e: In this way, freedom of heart comes from the fading away of greed, while freedom by wisdom comes from the fading away of ignorance.”
Numbered Discourses 2.32–41
The Chapter on the Peaceful Mind
“Mendicants, I will teach you the level of the untrue person and the level of the true person.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha. bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What is the level of the untrue person?
The untrue person is ungrateful and thankless,

segs.p: Asabbhi hetaṁ, bhikkhave, upaññātaṁ yadidaṁ akataññutā akataveditā.
segs.e: for the wicked only know how to be ungrateful and thankless.

segs.p: Kevalā esā, bhikkhave, asappurisabhūmi yadidaṁ akataññutā akataveditā. (…)
segs.e: It is totally the level of an untrue person to be ungrateful and thankless.

segs.p: Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, kataññū hoti katavedī.
segs.e: The true person is grateful and thankful,

segs.p: Sabbhi hetaṁ, bhikkhave, upaññātaṁ yadidaṁ kataññutā kataveditā.
segs.e: for the virtuous only know how to be grateful and thankful.

segs.p: Kevalā esā, bhikkhave, sappurisabhūmi yadidaṁ kataññutā kataveditā”ti.
segs.e: It is totally the level of a true person to be grateful and thankful.”
“Mendicants, I say that these two individuals cannot easily be repaid.
What two?
Mother and father.

segs.p: Ekena, bhikkhave, aṁsena mātaraṁ parihareyya, ekena aṁsena pitaraṁ parihareyya vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī so ca nesaṁ ucchādanaparimaddananhāpanasambāhanena.
segs.e: You would not have done enough to repay your mother and father even if you were to carry your mother around on one shoulder and your father on the other, and if you lived like this for a hundred years, and if you were to anoint, massage, bathe, and rub them;

segs.p: Te ca tattheva muttakarīsaṁ cajeyyuṁ, na tveva, bhikkhave, mātāpitūnaṁ kataṁ vā hoti paṭikataṁ vā.
segs.e: and even if they were to defecate and urinate right there.

segs.p: Imissā ca, bhikkhave, mahāpathaviyā pahūtarattaratanāya mātāpitaro issarādhipacce rajje patiṭṭhāpeyya, na tveva, bhikkhave, mātāpitūnaṁ kataṁ vā hoti paṭikataṁ vā.
segs.e: Even if you were to establish your mother and father as supreme monarchs of this great earth, abounding in the seven treasures, you would still not have done enough to repay them.
Why is that?

segs.p: Bahukārā, bhikkhave, mātāpitaro puttānaṁ āpādakā posakā imassa lokassa dassetāro.
segs.e: Parents are very helpful to their children: they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, mātāpitaro assaddhe saddhāsampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti, dussīle sīlasampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti, maccharī cāgasampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti, duppaññe paññāsampadāya samādapeti niveseti patiṭṭhāpeti, ettāvatā kho, bhikkhave, mātāpitūnaṁ katañca hoti paṭikatañcā”ti.
segs.e: But you have done enough, more than enough, to repay them if you encourage, settle, and ground unfaithful parents in faith, unethical parents in ethical conduct, stingy parents in generosity, or ignorant parents in wisdom.”

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him. When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,
“What does the worthy Gotama teach? What does he explain?”
“Brahmin, I teach action and inaction.”

segs.p: “Yathākathaṁ pana bhavaṁ gotamo kiriyavādī ca akiriyavādī cā”ti?
segs.e: “But in what way does the worthy Gotama teach action and inaction?”

segs.p: “Akiriyaṁ kho ahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vadāmi kāyaduccaritassa vacīduccaritassa manoduccaritassa, anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ akiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: “I teach inaction regarding bad bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, and the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Kiriyañca kho ahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vadāmi kāyasucaritassa vacīsucaritassa manosucaritassa, anekavihitānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ kiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: I teach action regarding good bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, and the many kinds of skillful things.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho ahaṁ, brāhmaṇa, kiriyavādī ca akiriyavādī cā”ti.
segs.e: This is the kind of action and inaction that I teach.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! … From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “kati nu kho, bhante, loke dakkhiṇeyyā, kattha ca dānaṁ dātabban”ti?
segs.e: “How many in the world are worthy of a religious donation? And where should a gift be given?”
“Householder, there are two in the world who are worthy of a religious donation:
the trainee and the adept.

segs.p: Ime kho, gahapati, dve loke dakkhiṇeyyā, ettha ca dānaṁ dātabban”ti.
segs.e: These two in the world are worthy of a religious donation, and that’s where you should give a gift.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“In this world, the trainee and the adept,
are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.
They are sincere in body,
speech, and mind.
This is the field for sponsors of sacrifice—
what’s given here is very fruitful.”
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:
“I will teach you about an individual fettered internally and one fettered externally.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:
“Who is an individual fettered internally?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: So tato cuto āgāmī hoti, āgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: When they pass away from there, they’re a returner, who comes back to this place.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, āvuso, ajjhattasaṁyojano puggalo āgāmī hoti, āgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: This is called an individual who is fettered internally, a returner, who comes back to this place.
Who is an individual fettered externally?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: So aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They enter and remain in a certain peaceful state of freed mind.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: So tato cuto anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: When they pass away from there, they’re a non-returner, not coming back to this place.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, bahiddhāsaṁyojano puggalo anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: This is called an individual who is fettered externally, a non-returner, who does not come back to this place.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical … they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: So kāmānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding sensual pleasures.

segs.p: So bhavānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding future lives.
They practice for the ending of craving.
They practice for the ending of greed.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: So tato cuto anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: When they pass away from there, they are non-returners, not coming back to this place.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, bahiddhāsaṁyojano puggalo anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattan”ti.
segs.e: This is called an individual who is fettered externally, a non-returner, who does not come back to this place.”

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā samacittā devatā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho tā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several peaceful-minded deities went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “eso, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde bhikkhūnaṁ ajjhattasaṁyojanañca puggalaṁ deseti bahiddhāsaṁyojanañca.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta is in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, where he is teaching the mendicants about an individual with internal fetters and one with external fetters.
The assembly is overjoyed!

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: Sir, please go to Venerable Sāriputta out of sympathy.”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—jetavane antarahito pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde āyasmato sāriputtassa sammukhe pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, in front of Sāriputta.
He sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Āyasmāpi kho sāriputto bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Sāriputta bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Idha, sāriputta, sambahulā samacittā devatā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, sāriputta, tā devatā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: “Just now, Sāriputta, several peaceful-minded deities came up to me, bowed, and stood to one side. Those deities said to me:

segs.p: ‘eso, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde bhikkhūnaṁ ajjhattasaṁyojanañca puggalaṁ deseti bahiddhāsaṁyojanañca.
segs.e: ‘Sir, Venerable Sāriputta is in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, where he is teaching the mendicants about an individual with internal fetters and one with external fetters.
The assembly is overjoyed!

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena āyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
segs.e: Sir, please go to Venerable Sāriputta out of sympathy.’

segs.p: Tā kho pana, sāriputta, devatā dasapi hutvā vīsampi hutvā tiṁsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā saṭṭhipi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti, na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhenti.
segs.e: Those deities, though they number ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or sixty, can stand on the point of a needle without bumping up against each other.
Sāriputta, you might think:

segs.p: ‘tattha nūna tāsaṁ devatānaṁ tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ yena tā devatā dasapi hutvā vīsampi hutvā tiṁsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā saṭṭhipi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Surely those deities, since so many of them can stand on the point of a needle without bumping up against each other, must have developed their minds in that place.’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, sāriputta, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like this.

segs.p: Idheva kho, sāriputta, tāsaṁ devatānaṁ tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ, yena tā devatā dasapi hutvā …pe… na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhenti.
segs.e: It was right here that those deities developed their minds.
So you should train like this:
‘We shall have peaceful faculties and peaceful minds.’
That’s how you should train.

segs.p: ‘Santindriyānañhi vo, sāriputta, santamānasānaṁ santaṁyeva kāyakammaṁ bhavissati santaṁ vacīkammaṁ santaṁ manokammaṁ.
segs.e: When your faculties and mind are peaceful, your acts of body, speech, and mind will be peaceful, thinking:
‘We shall present the gift of peace to our spiritual companions.’
That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Anassuṁ kho, sāriputta, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā ye imaṁ dhammapariyāyaṁ nāssosun’”ti.
segs.e: Those wanderers of other religions, Sāriputta, who have not heard this exposition of the teaching are lost.”
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno varaṇāyaṁ viharati bhaddasāritīre.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying at Varaṇā, on the bank of the Kaddama Lake.

segs.p: Atha kho ārāmadaṇḍo brāhmaṇo yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Ārāmadaṇḍa went up to Mahākaccāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho ārāmadaṇḍo brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Mahākaccāna:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho kaccāna, hetu ko paccayo yena khattiyāpi khattiyehi vivadanti, brāhmaṇāpi brāhmaṇehi vivadanti, gahapatikāpi gahapatikehi vivadantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Kaccāna, what is the reason why aristocrats fight with aristocrats, brahmins fight with brahmins, and householders fight with householders?”

segs.p: “Kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānahetu kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyāpi khattiyehi vivadanti, brāhmaṇāpi brāhmaṇehi vivadanti, gahapatikāpi gahapatikehi vivadantī”ti.
segs.e: “It is because of their insistence on sensual desire, their shackles, avarice, and attachment, that aristocrats fight with aristocrats, brahmins fight with brahmins, and householders fight with householders.”

segs.p: “Ko pana, bho kaccāna, hetu ko paccayo yena samaṇāpi samaṇehi vivadantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, worthy Kaccāna, what is the reason why ascetics fight with ascetics?”
“It is because of their insistence on views, their shackles, avarice, and attachment, that ascetics fight with ascetics.”

segs.p: “Atthi pana, bho kaccāna, koci lokasmiṁ yo imañceva kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto, imañca diṭṭhirāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Kaccāna, is there anyone in the world who has gone beyond the insistence on sensual desire and the insistence on views?”

segs.p: “Atthi, brāhmaṇa, lokasmiṁ yo imañceva kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto, imañca diṭṭhirāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto”ti.
segs.e: “There is, brahmin.”

segs.p: “Ko pana so, bho kaccāna, lokasmiṁ yo imañceva kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto, imañca diṭṭhirāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto”ti?
segs.e: “Who in the world has gone beyond the insistence on sensual desire and the insistence on views?”

segs.p: “Atthi, brāhmaṇa, puratthimesu janapadesu sāvatthī nāma nagaraṁ.
segs.e: “In the eastern lands there is a city named Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tattha so bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.
segs.e: There the Blessed One is now staying, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: So hi, brāhmaṇa, bhagavā imañceva kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto, imañca diṭṭhirāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto”ti.
segs.e: He, brahmin, has gone beyond the insistence on sensual desire and the insistence on views.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, ārāmadaṇḍo brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā dakkhiṇaṁ jāṇumaṇḍalaṁ pathaviyaṁ nihantvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: When this was said, the brahmin Ārāmadaṇḍa rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt on his right knee, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and expressed this heartfelt sentiment three times:
“Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

segs.p: Yo hi so bhagavā imañceva kāmarāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto, imañca diṭṭhirāgābhinivesavinibandhapaligedhapariyuṭṭhānajjhosānaṁ samatikkanto”ti.
segs.e: He who has gone beyond the insistence on sensual desire and the insistence on views.
Excellent, worthy Kaccāna! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho kaccāna, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya; andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā kaccānena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the worthy Kaccāna has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bho kaccāna, taṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ kaccāno dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Kaccāna remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākaccāno madhurāyaṁ viharati gundāvane.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākaccāna was staying near Madhurā in the Nut Grass Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho kandarāyano brāhmaṇo yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho kandarāyano brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahākaccānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the brahmin Kandarāyana went up to Mahākaccāna, and exchanged greetings with him … He sat down to one side and said to Mahākaccāna:

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bho kaccāna, ‘na samaṇo kaccāno brāhmaṇe jiṇṇe vuddhe mahallake addhagate vayoanuppatte abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimantetī’ti.
segs.e: “I have heard, worthy Kaccāna, that the ascetic Kaccāna doesn’t bow to old brahmins, the elderly and senior, who are advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life; nor does he rise in their presence or offer them a seat.
And this is indeed the case,

segs.p: Na hi bhavaṁ kaccāno brāhmaṇe jiṇṇe vuddhe mahallake addhagate vayoanuppatte abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimanteti.
segs.e: for the ascetic Kaccāna does not bow to old brahmins, elderly and senior, who are advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life; nor does he rise in their presence or offer them a seat.
This is not appropriate, worthy Kaccāna.”

segs.p: “Atthi, brāhmaṇa, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena vuddhabhūmi ca akkhātā daharabhūmi ca.
segs.e: “There is the stage of an elder and the stage of youth as explained by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Vuddho cepi, brāhmaṇa, hoti āsītiko vā nāvutiko vā vassasatiko vā jātiyā, so ca kāme paribhuñjati kāmamajjhāvasati kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhati kāmavitakkehi khajjati kāmapariyesanāya ussuko.
segs.e: If an elder, though eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, still dwells in the midst of sensual pleasures, enjoying them, consumed by thoughts of them, burning with fever for them, and eagerly seeking more,

segs.p: Atha kho so bālo na therotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: they are reckoned as a child, not a senior.

segs.p: Daharo cepi, brāhmaṇa, hoti yuvā susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā.
segs.e: If a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life,

segs.p: So ca na kāme paribhuñjati na kāmamajjhāvasati, na kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhati, na kāmavitakkehi khajjati, na kāmapariyesanāya ussuko.
segs.e: does not dwell in the midst of sensual pleasures, enjoying them, consumed by thoughts of them, burning with fever for them, and eagerly seeking more,

segs.p: Atha kho so paṇḍito therotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: they are reckoned as astute, a senior.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, kandarāyano brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā daharānaṁ sataṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pāde sirasā vandati:
segs.e: When this was said, the brahmin Kandarāyana got up from his seat, placed his robe over one shoulder, and bowed with his head to the feet of the young mendicants, saying,
“The good fellows are elders, at the stage of the elder;
we are youths, at the stage of youth.

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho kaccāna …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ kaccāno dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Kaccāna! … From this day forth, may the worthy Kaccāna remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye corā balavanto honti, rājāno tasmiṁ samaye dubbalā honti.
segs.e: “At a time when bandits are strong, kings are weak.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye rañño na phāsu hoti atiyātuṁ vā niyyātuṁ vā paccantime vā janapade anusaññātuṁ.
segs.e: Then the king is not at ease when going out or coming back or when touring the provinces.

segs.p: Brāhmaṇagahapatikānampi tasmiṁ samaye na phāsu hoti atiyātuṁ vā niyyātuṁ vā bāhirāni vā kammantāni paṭivekkhituṁ.
segs.e: The brahmins and householders, likewise, are not at ease when going out or coming back, or when inspecting their external business activities.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye pāpabhikkhū balavanto honti, pesalā bhikkhū tasmiṁ samaye dubbalā honti.
segs.e: In the same way, at a time when bad mendicants are strong, good-hearted mendicants are weak.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye pesalā bhikkhū tuṇhībhūtā tuṇhībhūtāva saṅghamajjhe saṅkasāyanti paccantime vā janapade acchanti.
segs.e: Then the good-hearted mendicants continually adhere to silence in the midst of the Saṅgha, or they stay in the borderlands.

segs.p: Tayidaṁ, bhikkhave, hoti bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: This is for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye rājāno balavanto honti, corā tasmiṁ samaye dubbalā honti.
segs.e: At a time when kings are strong, bandits are weak.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye rañño phāsu hoti atiyātuṁ vā niyyātuṁ vā paccantime vā janapade anusaññātuṁ.
segs.e: Then the king is at ease when going out or coming back or when inspecting the provinces.

segs.p: Brāhmaṇagahapatikānampi tasmiṁ samaye phāsu hoti atiyātuṁ vā niyyātuṁ vā bāhirāni vā kammantāni paṭivekkhituṁ.
segs.e: The brahmins and householders, likewise, are at ease when going out or coming back, or when inspecting their external business activities.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye pesalā bhikkhū balavanto honti, pāpabhikkhū tasmiṁ samaye dubbalā honti.
segs.e: In the same way, at a time when good-hearted mendicants are strong, bad mendicants are weak.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye pāpabhikkhū tuṇhībhūtā tuṇhībhūtāva saṅghamajjhe saṅkasāyanti, yena vā pana tena pakkamanti.
segs.e: Then the bad mendicants continually adhere to silence in the midst of the Saṅgha, or they leave for some place or other.

segs.p: Tayidaṁ, bhikkhave, hoti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: This is for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Dvinnāhaṁ, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipattiṁ na vaṇṇemi, gihissa vā pabbajitassa vā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I don’t praise wrong practice for these two, for laypeople and renunciates.

segs.p: Gihī vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu na ārādhako hoti ñāyaṁ dhammaṁ kusalaṁ.
segs.e: Because of wrong practice, neither laypeople nor renunciates succeed in completing the system of the skillful teaching.

segs.p: Dvinnāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipattiṁ vaṇṇemi, gihissa vā pabbajitassa vā.
segs.e: I praise right practice for these two, for laypeople and renunciates.

segs.p: Gihī vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṁ dhammaṁ kusalan”ti.
segs.e: Because of right practice, both laypeople and renunciates succeed in completing the system of the skillful teaching.”

segs.p: “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū duggahitehi suttantehi byañjanappatirūpakehi atthañca dhammañca paṭibāhanti te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanāhitāya paṭipannā bahujanāsukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, by memorizing the discourses incorrectly, taking only a semblance of the phrasing, some mendicants shut out the meaning and the teaching. They act for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū apuññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ antaradhāpenti.
segs.e: They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.

segs.p: Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suggahitehi suttantehi byañjanappatirūpakehi atthañca dhammañca anulomenti te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: But by memorizing the discourses well, not taking only a semblance of the phrasing, some mendicants conform to the meaning and the teaching. They act for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.
segs.e: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”
Numbered Discourses 2.42–51
The Chapter on Assemblies
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Uttānā ca parisā gambhīrā ca parisā.
segs.e: A shallow assembly and a deep assembly.
And what is a shallow assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū uddhatā honti unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants are haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.
This is called a shallow assembly.
And what is a deep assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū anuddhatā honti anunnaḷā acapalā amukharā avikiṇṇavācā upaṭṭhitassatī sampajānā samāhitā ekaggacittā saṁvutindriyā.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants are not haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, or loose-tongued, but have established mindfulness, situational awareness, immersion, unified minds, and restrained faculties.
This is called a deep assembly.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ gambhīrā parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the deep assembly.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Vaggā ca parisā samaggā ca parisā.
segs.e: A divided assembly and a harmonious assembly.
And what is a divided assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants fight, quarrel, and dispute, continually wounding each other with barbed words.
This is called a divided assembly.
And what is a harmonious assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṁ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants live in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes.
This is called a harmonious assembly.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ samaggā parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the harmonious assembly.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Anaggavatī ca parisā aggavatī ca parisā.
segs.e: An assembly of the worst and an assembly of the best.
And what is an assembly of the worst?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ therā bhikkhū bāhulikā honti sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: An assembly where the senior mendicants are indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti bāhulikā sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too become indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
This is called an assembly of the worst.
And what is an assembly of the best?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ therā bhikkhū na bāhulikā honti na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā, paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: An assembly where the senior mendicants are not indulgent or slack, nor are they backsliders; instead, they take the lead in seclusion, rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti na bāhulikā na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā, paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too are not indulgent or slack, nor are they backsliders; instead, they take the lead in seclusion, rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
This is called an assembly of the best.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ aggavatī parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly of the best.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Anariyā ca parisā ariyā ca parisā.
segs.e: An ignoble assembly and a noble assembly.
And what is an ignoble assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants don’t truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is called an ignoble assembly.
And what is a noble assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is called a noble assembly.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ ariyā parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the noble assembly.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?
An assembly of the dregs and an assembly of the cream.
And what is an assembly of the dregs?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū chandāgatiṁ gacchanti, dosāgatiṁ gacchanti, mohāgatiṁ gacchanti, bhayāgatiṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice.
This is called an assembly of the dregs.
And what is an assembly of the cream?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū na chandāgatiṁ gacchanti, na dosāgatiṁ gacchanti, na mohāgatiṁ gacchanti, na bhayāgatiṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: An assembly where the mendicants make decisions unprejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice.
This is called an assembly of the cream.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ parisāmaṇḍo”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly of the cream.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Okkācitavinītā parisā nopaṭipucchāvinītā, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā.
segs.e: An assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning, and an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, okkācitavinītā parisā nopaṭipucchāvinītā?
segs.e: And what is an assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatāpaṭisaṁyuttā tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsanti na sotaṁ odahanti na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
segs.e: It is an assembly where, when discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited the mendicants do not want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand, nor do they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

segs.p: Ye pana te suttantā kavitā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti, te ca taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā na ceva aññamaññaṁ paṭipucchanti na ca paṭivicaranti:
segs.e: But when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited the mendicants do want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand, and they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing. But when they’ve memorized those teachings they don’t question or examine each other, saying:
‘Why does it say this? What does that mean?’

segs.p: Te avivaṭañceva na vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca na uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ na paṭivinodenti.
segs.e: So they don’t reveal what is hidden or clarify what is unclear, or dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, okkācitavinītā parisā no paṭipucchāvinītā.
segs.e: This is called an assembly educated in fancy talk, not in questioning.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā?
segs.e: And what is an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū ye te suttantā kavitā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsanti na sotaṁ odahanti na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
segs.e: It is an assembly where, when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited the mendicants do not want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand, nor do they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

segs.p: Ye pana te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatāpaṭisaṁyuttā tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti, te ca dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññanti.
segs.e: But when discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited the mendicants do want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand, and they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

segs.p: Te taṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā aññamaññaṁ paṭipucchanti paṭivicaranti:
segs.e: And when they’ve memorized those teachings they question and examine each other, saying:
‘Why does it say this? What does that mean?’

segs.p: Te avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.
segs.e: So they reveal what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā.
segs.e: This is called an assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.
These are the two assemblies.
