segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ paṭipucchāvinītā parisā nookkācitavinītā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly educated in questioning, not in fancy talk.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Āmisagaru parisā no saddhammagaru, saddhammagaru parisā no āmisagaru.
segs.e: An assembly that values things of the flesh, not the true teaching, and an assembly that values the true teaching, not things of the flesh.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, āmisagaru parisā no saddhammagaru?
segs.e: And what is an assembly that values things of the flesh, not the true teaching?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū gihīnaṁ odātavasanānaṁ sammukhā aññamaññassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsanti:
segs.e: It is an assembly where the mendicants praise each other in front of the white-clothed laypeople, saying:

segs.p: ‘asuko bhikkhu ubhatobhāgavimutto, asuko paññāvimutto, asuko kāyasakkhī, asuko diṭṭhippatto, asuko saddhāvimutto, asuko dhammānusārī, asuko saddhānusārī, asuko sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, asuko dussīlo pāpadhammo’ti.
segs.e: ‘The mendicant so-and-so is freed both ways; so-and-so is freed by wisdom; so-and-so is a direct witness; so-and-so is attained to view; so-and-so is freed by faith; so-and-so is a follower of teachings; so-and-so is a follower by faith; so-and-so is ethical, of good character; so-and-so is unethical, of bad character.’
They thereby acquire material things.

segs.p: Te taṁ lābhaṁ labhitvā gathitā mucchitā ajjhopannā anādīnavadassāvino anissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti.
segs.e: And when they get these things, they use them tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, āmisagaru parisā no saddhammagaru.
segs.e: This is called an assembly that values things of the flesh, not the true teaching.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, saddhammagaru parisā noāmisagaru?
segs.e: And what is an assembly that values the true teaching, not things of the flesh?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū gihīnaṁ odātavasanānaṁ sammukhā aññamaññassa vaṇṇaṁ na bhāsanti:
segs.e: It is an assembly where the mendicants don’t praise each other in front of the white-clothed laypeople, saying:

segs.p: ‘asuko bhikkhu ubhatobhāgavimutto, asuko paññāvimutto, asuko kāyasakkhī, asuko diṭṭhippatto, asuko saddhāvimutto, asuko dhammānusārī, asuko saddhānusārī, asuko sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, asuko dussīlo pāpadhammo’ti.
segs.e: ‘The mendicant so-and-so is freed both ways; so-and-so is freed by wisdom; so-and-so is a direct witness; so-and-so is attained to view; so-and-so is freed by faith; so-and-so is a follower of teachings; so-and-so is a follower by faith; so-and-so is ethical, of good character; so-and-so is unethical, of bad character.’
They thereby acquire material things.

segs.p: Te taṁ lābhaṁ labhitvā agathitā amucchitā anajjhosannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti.
segs.e: And when they get these things, they use them untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, saddhammagaru parisā noāmisagaru.
segs.e: This is called an assembly that values the true teaching, not things of the flesh.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ saddhammagaru parisā noāmisagarū”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly that values the true teaching, not things of the flesh.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Visamā ca parisā samā ca parisā.
segs.e: An unjust assembly and a just assembly.
And what is an unjust assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ adhammakammāni pavattanti dhammakammāni nappavattanti, avinayakammāni pavattanti vinayakammāni nappavattanti, adhammakammāni dippanti dhammakammāni na dippanti, avinayakammāni dippanti vinayakammāni na dippanti.
segs.e: An assembly where legal acts against the teaching proceed, while legal acts following the teaching don’t proceed. Legal acts against the training proceed, while legal acts following the training don’t proceed. Legal acts against the teaching are explained, while legal acts following the teaching aren’t explained. Legal acts against the training are explained, while legal acts following the training aren’t explained.
This is called an unjust assembly.
And what is a just assembly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ dhammakammāni pavattanti adhammakammāni nappavattanti, vinayakammāni pavattanti avinayakammāni nappavattanti, dhammakammāni dippanti adhammakammāni na dippanti, vinayakammāni dippanti avinayakammāni na dippanti.
segs.e: An assembly where legal acts following the teaching proceed, while legal acts against the teaching don’t proceed. Legal acts following the training proceed, while legal acts against the training don’t proceed. Legal acts following the teaching are explained, while legal acts against the teaching aren’t explained. Legal acts in line with the training are explained, while legal acts following training aren’t explained.
This is called a just assembly.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ samā parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the just assembly.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Adhammikā ca parisā dhammikā ca parisā …pe… imā kho, bhikkhave, dve parisā.
segs.e: An unprincipled assembly and a principled assembly …

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammikā parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the principled assembly.”
“There are, mendicants, these two assemblies.
What two?

segs.p: Adhammavādinī ca parisā dhammavādinī ca parisā.
segs.e: An assembly with unprincipled speech, and an assembly with principled speech.
And what is an assembly with unprincipled speech?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyanti dhammikaṁ vā adhammikaṁ vā.
segs.e: It is an assembly where the mendicants take up disciplinary issues, whether legitimate or not.

segs.p: Te taṁ adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyitvā na ceva aññamaññaṁ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṁ upagacchanti, na ca nijjhāpenti na ca nijjhattiṁ upagacchanti.
segs.e: But they don’t persuade each other or allow themselves to be persuaded, nor do they convince each other or allow themselves to be convinced.

segs.p: Te asaññattibalā anijjhattibalā appaṭinissaggamantino tameva adhikaraṇaṁ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharanti:
segs.e: Unable to persuade or convince each other, they can’t let go of their opinions. They obstinately stick to that disciplinary issue, insisting that:
‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
This is called an assembly with unprincipled speech.
And what is an assembly with principled speech?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yassaṁ parisāyaṁ bhikkhū adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyanti dhammikaṁ vā adhammikaṁ vā.
segs.e: It is an assembly where the mendicants take up disciplinary issues, whether legitimate or not.

segs.p: Te taṁ adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyitvā aññamaññaṁ saññāpenti ceva saññattiñca upagacchanti, nijjhāpenti ceva nijjhattiñca upagacchanti.
segs.e: Then they persuade each other or allow themselves to be persuaded, and they convince each other or allow themselves to be convinced.

segs.p: Te saññattibalā nijjhattibalā paṭinissaggamantino, na tameva adhikaraṇaṁ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharanti:
segs.e: Since they are able to persuade and convince each other, they let go of their opinions. They don’t obstinately stick to that disciplinary issue or insist that:
‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
This is called an assembly with principled speech.
These are the two assemblies.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ dvinnaṁ parisānaṁ yadidaṁ dhammavādinī parisā”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two assemblies is the assembly with principled speech.”
Numbered Discourses 2.52–63
The Chapter on Individuals

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “These two individuals, mendicants, arise in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
What two?

segs.p: Tathāgato ca arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, rājā ca cakkavattī.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha; and the wheel-turning monarch.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who arise in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti acchariyamanussā.
segs.e: “These two individuals, mendicants, arise in the world who are incredible human beings.
What two?

segs.p: Tathāgato ca arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, rājā ca cakkavattī.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha; and the wheel-turning monarch.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā loke uppajjamānā uppajjanti acchariyamanussā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who arise in the world who are incredible human beings.”

segs.p: “Dvinnaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalānaṁ kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hoti.
segs.e: “There are two individuals, mendicants, whose death is regretted by many people.
What two?

segs.p: Tathāgatassa ca arahato sammāsambuddhassa, rañño ca cakkavattissa.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha; and the wheel-turning monarch.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ puggalānaṁ kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hotī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals, mendicants, whose death is regretted by many people.”
“Mendicants, these two are worthy of a monument.
What two?

segs.p: Tathāgato ca arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, rājā ca cakkavattī.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha; and the wheel-turning monarch.
These are the two who are worthy of a monument.”
“Mendicants, there are two kinds of Buddhas.
What two?

segs.p: Tathāgato ca arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, paccekabuddho ca.
segs.e: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha; and an independent Buddha.
These are the two kinds of Buddhas.”
“These two, mendicants, are not startled by a crack of thunder.
What two?
A mendicant who has ended defilements; and a thoroughbred elephant.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve asaniyā phalantiyā na santasantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two who are not startled by a crack of thunder.”
“These two, mendicants, are not startled by a crack of thunder.
What two?
A mendicant who has ended defilements; and a thoroughbred horse.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve asaniyā phalantiyā na santasantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two who are not startled by a crack of thunder.”
“These two, mendicants, are not startled by a crack of thunder.
What two?

segs.p: Bhikkhu ca khīṇāsavo, sīho ca migarājā.
segs.e: A mendicant who has ended defilements; and a lion, king of beasts.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve asaniyā phalantiyā na santasantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two who are not startled by a crack of thunder.”

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, atthavase sampassamānā kiṁpurisā mānusiṁ vācaṁ na bhāsanti.
segs.e: “Mystery men see two reasons not to use regular speech.
What two?

segs.p: Mā ca musā bhaṇimhā, mā ca paraṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhimhāti.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘May we not lie, and may we not misrepresent others with falsehoods.’

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve atthavase sampassamānā kiṁpurisā mānusiṁ vācaṁ na bhāsantī”ti.
segs.e: Mystery men see these two reasons not to use regular speech.”

segs.p: “Dvinnaṁ dhammānaṁ, bhikkhave, atitto appaṭivāno mātugāmo kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, ladies die without getting enough of two things.
What two?
Sexual intercourse and giving birth.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ dhammānaṁ atitto appaṭivāno mātugāmo kālaṁ karotī”ti.
segs.e: Ladies die without getting enough of these two things.”
“Mendicants, I will teach you about living with bad people and living with good people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Kathañca, bhikkhave, asantasannivāso hoti, kathañca asanto sannivasanti?
segs.e: “What is it like living with bad people? How do bad people live together?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, therassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a senior mendicant thinks:

segs.p: ‘theropi maṁ na vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ na vadeyya, navopi maṁ na vadeyya;
segs.e: ‘No mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

segs.p: therampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ.
segs.e: and I shouldn’t admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

segs.p: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they wouldn’t be sympathetic, and I’d bother them by saying “No!” And anyway I wouldn’t deal with it even if I saw what I did wrong.’

segs.p: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya, ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ’.
Majjhimassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti …pe… navassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

segs.p: ‘theropi maṁ na vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ na vadeyya, navopi maṁ na vadeyya;
segs.e: ‘No mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

segs.p: therampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ na vadeyyaṁ.
segs.e: and I shouldn’t admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

segs.p: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they wouldn’t be sympathetic, and I’d bother them by saying “No!” And anyway I wouldn’t deal with it even if I saw what I did wrong.’

segs.p: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya … navo cepi maṁ vadeyya ahitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no hitānukampī, noti naṁ vadeyyaṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa nappaṭikareyyaṁ’.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, asantasannivāso hoti, evañca asanto sannivasanti.
segs.e: That’s what it’s like living with bad people; that’s how bad people live together.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, santasannivāso hoti, kathañca santo sannivasanti?
segs.e: What is it like living with good people? How do good people live together?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, therassa bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a senior mendicant thinks:

segs.p: ‘theropi maṁ vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ vadeyya, navopi maṁ vadeyya;
segs.e: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

segs.p: therampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ.
segs.e: and I should admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

segs.p: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

segs.p: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ’.
Majjhimassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti …pe… navassapi bhikkhuno evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

segs.p: ‘theropi maṁ vadeyya, majjhimopi maṁ vadeyya, navopi maṁ vadeyya;
segs.e: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, may admonish me;

segs.p: therampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, majjhimampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ, navampāhaṁ vadeyyaṁ.
segs.e: and I’ll admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

segs.p: Thero cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ.
segs.e: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

segs.p: Majjhimo cepi maṁ vadeyya …pe… navo cepi maṁ vadeyya hitānukampī maṁ vadeyya no ahitānukampī, sādhūti naṁ vadeyyaṁ na naṁ viheṭheyyaṁ passampissa paṭikareyyaṁ’.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, santasannivāso hoti, evañca santo sannivasantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s what it’s like living with good people; that’s how good people live together.”

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe ubhato vacīsaṁsāro diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi ajjhattaṁ avūpasantaṁ hoti, tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: “In any disciplinary issue where on both sides the endless talk, contempt for each other’s views, resentment, bitterness, and exasperation is not settled, you can expect that this disciplinary issue

segs.p: ‘dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca na phāsuṁ viharissanti’.
segs.e: will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will not live comfortably.

segs.p: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe ubhato vacīsaṁsāro diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi ajjhattaṁ suvūpasantaṁ hoti, tasmetaṁ, bhikkhave, adhikaraṇe pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: In any disciplinary issue where on both sides the endless talk, contempt for each other’s views, resentment, bitterness, and exasperation is well settled, you can expect that this disciplinary issue

segs.p: ‘na dīghattāya kharattāya vāḷattāya saṁvattissati, bhikkhū ca phāsuṁ viharissantī’”ti.
segs.e: won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.”
Numbered Discourses 2.64–76
The Chapter on Happiness
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
The happiness of laypeople, and the happiness of renunciates.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ pabbajitasukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of renunciates.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Sensual happiness and the happiness of renunciation.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ nekkhammasukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of renunciation.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
The happiness of attachments, and the happiness of no attachments.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ nirupadhisukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of no attachments.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Defiled happiness and undefiled happiness.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ anāsavasukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of no defilements.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness of the flesh and happiness not of the flesh.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ nirāmisaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness not of the flesh.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Noble happiness and ignoble happiness.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ ariyasukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is noble happiness.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Physical happiness and mental happiness.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ cetasikaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is mental happiness.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness with rapture and happiness free of rapture.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ nippītikaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness free of rapture.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness with pleasure and happiness with equanimity.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ upekkhāsukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness with equanimity.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
The happiness of immersion and the happiness without immersion.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ samādhisukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of immersion.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness that relies on rapture and happiness that relies on freedom from rapture.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ nippītikārammaṇaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on freedom from rapture.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness that relies on pleasure and happiness that relies on equanimity.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ upekkhārammaṇaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on equanimity.”
“There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.
What two?
Happiness that relies on form and happiness that relies on the formless.
These are the two kinds of happiness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ dvinnaṁ sukhānaṁ yadidaṁ arūpārammaṇaṁ sukhan”ti.
segs.e: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on the formless.”
Numbered Discourses 2.77–86
The Chapter with a Basis

segs.p: “Sanimittā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no animittā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a basis, not without a basis.

segs.p: Tasseva nimittassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that basis, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sanidānā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no anidānā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a source, not without a source.

segs.p: Tasseva nidānassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that source, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sahetukā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no ahetukā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a cause, not without a cause.

segs.p: Tasseva hetussa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that cause, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sasaṅkhārā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no asaṅkhārā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with conditions, not without conditions.

segs.p: Tesaṁyeva saṅkhārānaṁ pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up those conditions, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sappaccayā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no appaccayā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a reason, not without a reason.

segs.p: Tasseva paccayassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that reason, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sarūpā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no arūpā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with form, not without form.

segs.p: Tasseva rūpassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that form, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Savedanā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no avedanā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with feeling, not without feeling.

segs.p: Tassāyeva vedanāya pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that feeling, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Sasaññā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no asaññā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with perception, not without perception.

segs.p: Tassāyeva saññāya pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that perception, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Saviññāṇā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no aviññāṇā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with consciousness, not without consciousness.

segs.p: Tasseva viññāṇassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that consciousness, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

segs.p: “Saṅkhatārammaṇā, bhikkhave, uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, no asaṅkhatārammaṇā.
segs.e: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a conditioned basis, not without a conditioned basis.

segs.p: Tasseva saṅkhatassa pahānā evaṁ te pāpakā akusalā dhammā na hontī”ti.
segs.e: By giving up that conditioned basis, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”
Numbered Discourses 2.87–97
The Chapter on Two Things
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Exertion, and not being scattered.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Name and form.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Knowledge and freedom.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Views favoring existence and views favoring nonexistence.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Lack of conscience and prudence.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Conscience and prudence.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Being hard to admonish and having bad friends.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Being easy to admonish and having good friends.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Skill in the elements and skill in application of mind.
These are the two things.”
“There are, mendicants, these two things.
What two?
Skill in offenses and skill in resolving offenses.
These are the two things.”
Numbered Discourses 2.98–117
The Chapter on Fools
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca anāgataṁ bhāraṁ vahati, yo ca āgataṁ bhāraṁ na vahati.
segs.e: One who carries the burden of what has not come to pass, and one who doesn’t carry the burden of what has come to pass.
These are the two fools.”
“There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca anāgataṁ bhāraṁ na vahati, yo ca āgataṁ bhāraṁ vahati.
segs.e: One who doesn’t carry the burden of what has not come to pass, and one who carries the burden of what has come to pass.
These are the two who are astute.”
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca akappiye kappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye akappiyasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is unallowable as allowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as unallowable.
These are the two fools.”
“There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca akappiye akappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye kappiyasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is unallowable as unallowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as allowable.
These are the two who are astute.”
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca anāpattiyā āpattisaññī, yo ca āpattiyā anāpattisaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives a non-offense as an offense, and one who perceives an offense as a non-offense.
These are the two fools.”
“There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca anāpattiyā anāpattisaññī, yo ca āpattiyā āpattisaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense, and one who perceives an offense as an offense.
These are the two who are astute.”
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca adhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme adhammasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives the teaching as not the teaching.
These are the two fools.”
“There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca dhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca adhamme adhammasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives what is not the teaching as not the teaching.
These are the two who are astute.”
“Mendicants, there are two fools.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca avinaye vinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye avinayasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the training as the training, and one who perceives what is the training as not the training.
These are the two fools.”
“There are two who are astute.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca avinaye avinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye vinayasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the training as not the training, and one who perceives what is the training as the training.
These are the two who are astute.”
“For these two, defilements grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca na kukkuccāyitabbaṁ kukkuccāyati, yo ca kukkuccāyitabbaṁ na kukkuccāyati.
segs.e: One who is remorseful over something they shouldn’t be, and one who isn’t remorseful over something they should be.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements grow.”
“For these two, defilements don’t grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca na kukkuccāyitabbaṁ na kukkuccāyati, yo ca kukkuccāyitabbaṁ kukkuccāyati.
segs.e: One who isn’t remorseful over something they shouldn’t be, and one who is remorseful over something they should be.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā na vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”
“For these two, defilements grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca akappiye kappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye akappiyasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is unallowable as allowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as unallowable.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements grow.”
“For these two, defilements don’t grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca akappiye akappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye kappiyasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is unallowable as unallowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as allowable.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā na vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”
“For these two, defilements grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca āpattiyā anāpattisaññī, yo ca anāpattiyā āpattisaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives an offense as a non-offense, and one who perceives a non-offense as an offense.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements grow.”
“For these two, defilements don’t grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca āpattiyā āpattisaññī, yo ca anāpattiyā anāpattisaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives an offense as an offense, and one who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā na vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”
“For these two, defilements grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca adhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme adhammasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives the teaching as not the teaching.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements grow.”
“For these two, defilements don’t grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca dhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca adhamme adhammasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives what is not the teaching as not the teaching.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā na vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”
“For these two, defilements grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca avinaye vinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye avinayasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the training as the training, and one who perceives what is the training as not the training.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements grow.”
“For these two, defilements don’t grow.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca avinaye avinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye vinayasaññī.
segs.e: One who perceives what is not the training as not the training, and one who perceives what is the training as the training.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ āsavā na vaḍḍhantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”
Numbered Discourses 2.118–129
The Chapter on Hopes That Are Hard to Give Up
“These two hopes are hard to give up.
What two?
The hope for wealth and the hope for long life.

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, dve āsā duppajahā”ti.
segs.e: These are two hopes that are hard to give up.”
“These two individuals are rare in the world.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca pubbakārī, yo ca kataññū katavedī.
segs.e: One who takes the initiative, and one who is grateful and thankful.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā dullabhā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who are rare in the world.”
“These two individuals are rare in the world.
What two?
One who is satisfied, and one who satisfies others.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā dullabhā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who are rare in the world.”
“These two individuals are hard to satisfy in the world.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca laddhaṁ laddhaṁ nikkhipati, yo ca laddhaṁ laddhaṁ vissajjeti.
segs.e: One who continually hoards wealth, and one who continually wastes wealth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā duttappayā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who are hard to satisfy in the world.”
“These two individuals are easy to satisfy in the world.
What two?

segs.p: Yo ca laddhaṁ laddhaṁ na nikkhipati, yo ca laddhaṁ laddhaṁ na vissajjeti.
segs.e: One who does not continually hoard wealth, and one who does not continually waste wealth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā sutappayā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two individuals who are easy to satisfy in the world.”
“There are two conditions for the arising of greed.
What two?
The feature of beauty and irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paccayā rāgassa uppādāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two conditions for the arising of greed.”
“There are two conditions for the arising of hate.
What two?
The feature of harshness and irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paccayā dosassa uppādāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two conditions for the arising of hate.”
“There are two conditions for the arising of wrong view.
What two?

segs.p: Parato ca ghoso ayoniso ca manasikāro.
segs.e: The voice of another and irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paccayā micchādiṭṭhiyā uppādāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two conditions for the arising of wrong view.”
“There are two conditions for the arising of right view.
What two?

segs.p: Parato ca ghoso, yoniso ca manasikāro.
segs.e: The voice of another and rational application of mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two conditions for the arising of right view.”
“There are these two offenses.
What two?

segs.p: Lahukā ca āpatti, garukā ca āpatti.
segs.e: A light offense and a heavy offense.
These are the two offenses.”
“There are these two offenses.
What two?

segs.p: Duṭṭhullā ca āpatti, aduṭṭhullā ca āpatti.
segs.e: An offense with corrupt intention and an offense without corrupt intention.
These are the two offenses.”
“There are these two offenses.
What two?

segs.p: Sāvasesā ca āpatti, anavasesā ca āpatti.
segs.e: A curable offense and an incurable offense.
These are the two offenses.”
Numbered Discourses 2.130–140
The Chapter on Aspiration

segs.p: “Saddho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ sammā āyācamāno āyāceyya:
segs.e: “A faithful monk would rightly aspire:
‘May I be like Sāriputta and Moggallāna!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ yadidaṁ sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my monk disciples, that is, Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”

segs.p: “Saddhā, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī evaṁ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya:
segs.e: “A faithful nun would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādisī homi yādisī khemā ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvikānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ yadidaṁ khemā ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā cā”ti.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my nun disciples, that is, the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā.”

segs.p: “Saddho, bhikkhave, upāsako evaṁ sammā āyācamāno āyāceyya:
segs.e: “A faithful layman would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādiso homi yādiso citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ yadidaṁ citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako”ti.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my male lay followers, that is, the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.”

segs.p: “Saddhā, bhikkhave, upāsikā evaṁ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya:
segs.e: “A faithful laywoman would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādisī homi yādisī khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā ca nandamātā’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvikānaṁ upāsikānaṁ yadidaṁ khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā ca nandamātā”ti.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my female lay disciples, that is, the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother.”

segs.p: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has two qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.
What two?
Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism
and they criticize those deserving of praise.

segs.e: Freedom from anger and acrimony … freedom from disdain and contempt … freedom from jealousy and stinginess … freedom from deceit and deviousness … conscience and prudence.

segs.e: When they have these two things, some people—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”
Numbered Discourses 2.230–279
The Chapter of Abbreviated Texts Beginning With the Unskillful

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā akusalā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā kusalā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā sāvajjā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā anavajjā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā dukkhudrayā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā sukhudrayā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā dukkhavipākā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā sukhavipākā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā sabyābajjhā … dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā abyābajjhā.
segs.e: “These two things are unskillful … are skillful … are blameworthy … are blameless … have suffering as outcome … have happiness as outcome … result in suffering … result in happiness … are hurtful … are not hurtful.
What two?

segs.p: Akkodho ca anupanāho ca … amakkho ca apaḷāso ca … anissā ca amacchariyañca … amāyā ca asāṭheyyañca … hirī ca ottappañca.
segs.e: Freedom from anger and acrimony … freedom from disdain and contempt … freedom from jealousy and stinginess … freedom from deceit and deviousness … conscience and prudence.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā abyābajjhā”ti.
segs.e: These are the two things that are not hurtful.”
Numbered Discourses 2.280–309
The Chapter of Abbreviated Texts on Monastic Law

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ.
segs.e: “For two reasons the Realized One laid down training rules for his disciples.
What two?

segs.p: Saṅghasuṭṭhutāya saṅghaphāsutāya … dummaṅkūnaṁ puggalānaṁ niggahāya, pesalānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ phāsuvihārāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ āsavānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ āsavānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ verānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ verānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ vajjānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ vajjānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ bhayānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ bhayānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭighātāya … gihīnaṁ anukampāya, pāpicchānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pakkhupacchedāya … appasannānaṁ pasādāya, pasannānaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya … saddhammaṭṭhitiyā vinayānuggahāya.
segs.e: For the well-being and comfort of the Saṅgha … For keeping difficult individuals in check and for the comfort of good-hearted mendicants … For restraining defilements that affect this life and protecting against defilements that affect lives to come … For restraining threats to this life and protecting against threats to lives to come … For restraining faults that affect this life and protecting against faults that affect lives to come … For restraining hazards that affect this life and protecting against hazards that affect lives to come … For restraining unskillful qualities that affect this life and protecting against unskillful qualities that affect lives to come … Out of sympathy for laypeople and for breaking up factions of mendicants with corrupt wishes … For inspiring confidence in those without it, and increasing confidence in those who have it … For the continuation of the true teaching and the support of the training.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattan”ti.
segs.e: These are the two reasons why the Realized One laid down training rules for his disciples.”

segs.p: “Dveme, bhikkhave, atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṁ pātimokkhaṁ paññattaṁ …pe… pātimokkhuddeso paññatto … pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṁ paññattaṁ … pavāraṇā paññattā … pavāraṇaṭṭhapanaṁ paññattaṁ … tajjanīyakammaṁ paññattaṁ … niyassakammaṁ paññattaṁ … pabbājanīyakammaṁ paññattaṁ … paṭisāraṇīyakammaṁ paññattaṁ … ukkhepanīyakammaṁ paññattaṁ … parivāsadānaṁ paññattaṁ … mūlāyapaṭikassanaṁ paññattaṁ … mānattadānaṁ paññattaṁ … abbhānaṁ paññattaṁ … osāraṇīyaṁ paññattaṁ … nissāraṇīyaṁ paññattaṁ … upasampadā paññattā … ñattikammaṁ paññattaṁ … ñattidutiyakammaṁ paññattaṁ … ñatticatutthakammaṁ paññattaṁ … apaññatte paññattaṁ … paññatte anupaññattaṁ … sammukhāvinayo paññatto … sativinayo paññatto … amūḷhavinayo paññatto … paṭiññātakaraṇaṁ paññattaṁ … yebhuyyasikā paññattā … tassapāpiyasikā paññattā … tiṇavatthārako paññatto.
segs.e: “For two reasons the Realized One laid down for his disciples the monastic code … the recitation of the monastic code … the suspension of the recitation of the monastic code … the invitation to admonish … the setting aside of the invitation to admonish … the disciplinary act of condemnation … placing under dependence … banishment … reconciliation … debarment … probation … being sent back to the beginning … penance … reinstatement … restoration … removal … ordination … an act with a motion … an act with a motion and one announcement … an act with a motion and three announcements … laying down what was not previously laid down … amending what was laid down … the settling of a disciplinary matter by the following methods: face-to-face … through recollection … because of past insanity … acting according to what has been admitted … majority decision … further penalty …  covering over as if with grass.
What two?

segs.p: Saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya … dummaṅkūnaṁ puggalānaṁ niggahāya, pesalānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ phāsuvihārāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ āsavānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ āsavānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ verānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ verānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ vajjānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ vajjānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ bhayānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ bhayānaṁ paṭighātāya … diṭṭhadhammikānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ saṁvarāya, samparāyikānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭighātāya … gihīnaṁ anukampāya, pāpicchānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ pakkhupacchedāya … appasannānaṁ pasādāya, pasannānaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya … saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya.
segs.e: For the well-being and comfort of the Saṅgha … For keeping difficult individuals in check and for the comfort of good-hearted mendicants … For restraining defilements that affect this life and protecting against defilements that affect lives to come … For restraining threats to this life and protecting against threats to lives to come … For restraining faults that affect this life and protecting against faults that affect lives to come … For restraining hazards that affect this life and protecting against hazards that affect lives to come … For restraining unskillful qualities that affect this life and protecting against unskillful qualities that affect lives to come … Out of sympathy for laypeople and for breaking up factions of mendicants with corrupt wishes … For inspiring confidence in those without it, and increasing confidence in those who have it … For the continuation of the true teaching and the support of the training.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṁ tiṇavatthārako paññatto”ti.
segs.e: These are the two reasons why the Realized One laid down the settlement of a disciplinary matter by covering over with grass for his disciples.”
Numbered Discourses 2.310–479
The Chapter of Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
“For insight into greed, two things should be developed.
What two?
Serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dve dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these two things should be developed.”

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, pariññāya … parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya dve dhammā bhāvetabbā …pe…
segs.e: “For the complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go of greed, two things should be developed.”

segs.p: “Dosassa …pe… mohassa … kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa … abhiññāya … pariññāya … parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya dve dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “Of hate … delusion … anger … acrimony … disdain … contempt … jealousy … stinginess … deceit … deviousness … obstinacy … aggression … conceit … arrogance … vanity … negligence … for insight … complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go … two things should be developed.
What two?
Serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Pamādassa, bhikkhave, paṭinissaggāya ime dve dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For the letting go of negligence, these two things should be developed.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
The Book of the Twos is finished.
